title: "Reproducible offline reads and the raw-file cache"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Reproducible offline reads and the raw-file cache}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  prompt = FALSE
)
library(readjsa)

fixture <- function(name) {
  installed <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "readjsa")
  candidates <- c(
    installed,
    file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", name),
    file.path("inst", "extdata", name)
  )
  path <- candidates[nzchar(candidates) & file.exists(candidates)]
  if (!length(path)) stop("The packaged fixture is missing: ", name)
  path[[1L]]
}
```

`readjsa` treats a raw release and its metadata as one reproducibility unit.
The cache key includes the release identity, parser version, and schema
version. A cache hit is accepted only after the file size, SHA-256, metadata,
official final URL, parser/schema versions, and age bounds are checked. The
default cache location is returned by `jsa_cache_dir()` and is managed with
`tools::R_user_dir()`.

```{r cache-location}
cache_path <- jsa_cache_dir()
stopifnot(is.character(cache_path), length(cache_path) == 1L, nzchar(cache_path))
cat("A platform-specific user cache path was returned.\n")
```

Local file reads do not need the cache. They still attach the exact local byte
count and SHA-256, so a report can record what was parsed.

```{r local-provenance}
local_ivi <- read_ivi_file(
  fixture("ivi_skill_states.xlsx"), family = "skill_states"
)
local_ivi[1, c(
  "family_id", "source_filename", "raw_bytes", "raw_sha256",
  "parser_version", "schema_version", "revision_policy"
)]
```

## Exercise a cache replay offline

The following example uses a custom transport that copies a packaged fixture
instead of opening a network connection. It still calls the real
`fetch_jsa_release()` cache implementation: the source URL is an official
HTTPS URL from the offline catalogue, the copied bytes are hashed, and the
second call must revalidate the cached pair without invoking the transport.

```{r offline-cache}
ivi_catalogue <- discover_jsa_releases(
  "ivi", html = fixture("ivi.html")
)
release <- ivi_catalogue[
  ivi_catalogue$family_id == "skill_states", , drop = FALSE
]

run_cache_demo <- function(release, source_file) {
  cache_dir <- tempfile("readjsa-cache-")
  dir.create(cache_dir)
  on.exit(unlink(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)

  transport_calls <- 0L
  transport <- function(url, destination, timeout, max_bytes) {
    transport_calls <<- transport_calls + 1L
    if (!file.copy(source_file, destination, overwrite = TRUE)) {
      stop("fixture transport could not create the destination")
    }
    invisible(url)
  }

  first <- fetch_jsa_release(
    release, cache_dir = cache_dir, transport = transport
  )
  second <- fetch_jsa_release(
    release, cache_dir = cache_dir, transport = transport
  )

  provenance_fields <- c(
    "provider_id", "dataset_id", "family_id", "release_id",
    "reference_period", "release_date", "vintage_date",
    "page_modified_date", "retrieved_at", "source_url", "final_url",
    "source_filename", "page_url", "raw_bytes", "raw_sha256",
    "parser_version", "schema_version", "revision_policy", "terms_url",
    "licence", "attribution"
  )
  parsed <- read_ivi_file(
    first$path,
    family = first$family_id,
    provenance = first[intersect(names(first), provenance_fields)]
  )

  list(
    cache = data.frame(
      transport_calls = transport_calls,
      first_cache_hit = first$cache_hit,
      second_cache_hit = second$cache_hit,
      raw_bytes = first$raw_bytes,
      sha256_prefix = substr(first$raw_sha256, 1L, 12L),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ),
    parsed = data.frame(
      rows = nrow(parsed),
      first_date = min(parsed$date),
      last_date = max(parsed$date),
      source_filename = parsed$source_filename[[1L]],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}

cache_demo <- run_cache_demo(
  release,
  fixture("ivi_skill_states.xlsx")
)
cache_demo$cache
cache_demo$parsed
```

The expected pattern is one transport call, `FALSE` for the first cache-hit
flag, and `TRUE` for the second. The SHA-256 prefix is shown only to keep the
article compact; production records should retain the complete hash. The
temporary cache is deleted at the end of the chunk, so this demonstration does
not alter a user's persistent cache.

High-level readers normally return no cache-diagnostic attribute. For an
instrumented run, set `READJSA_MEASUREMENT_CACHE_AUDIT=true`; the result then
has a logical `readjsa_raw_cache_hits` attribute with one observed outcome per
fetched release. This opt-in attribute does not add or reorder data-frame
columns. Unset the variable for ordinary workflows.

## Pinning a replay

For a report or pipeline, save at least the selected catalogue row and the
complete `raw_sha256` from the parsed output. The row identifies the provider,
dataset/family, reference period, source URL and terms; the hash identifies the
exact bytes. Re-running `read_*()` later may discover a newer release, whereas
replaying the saved raw file with `read_*_file()` preserves the original
vintage.

The cache is a convenience, not a data archive. It has bounded age, file count,
and total bytes, and a changed parser or schema version invalidates a hit. Keep
durable raw files and catalogue records outside the cache when long-term audit
or publication reproducibility is required.
